body.statement:
For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), put
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4,
 \qquad
 M_{k,\ell}=M_A+M_B.                                      \tag{18}
\]
The design-A and design-B coarse structural-mode enumerations used by \(\mathscr A\) have at most \(M_A\) and \(M_B\) templates, respectively.  Every template has a semialgebraic description with at most
\[
 N_0=4\ell+10k+12,
 \qquad
 S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1),
 \qquad
 D_0=4                                                     \tag{19}
\]
variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree.

Let \(\mathsf{Comp}\), \(\mathsf{Proj}\), and \(\mathsf{Lab}\) be coordinatewise nondecreasing versions of the explicit published output-format bounds for, respectively, the connected-component-description and sampling algorithm, the subsequent one-block projection and realizability algorithm, and the real-univariate, Thom-sign, and root-isolation algorithms invoked in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\).  A component record uses the original ambient variables and at most one real-univariate primitive-element coordinate for its sample; projection retains only the two target variables.  Define the bounds sequentially by
\[
 (A_C,S_C,D_C)=\mathsf{Comp}(N_0,S_0,D_0),
 \qquad
 Q_C=(N_0+3,S_C+3,2D_C+2),                                \tag{20}
\]
\[
 (A_P,S_P,D_P)=\mathsf{Proj}(Q_C;2),
 \qquad
 Q_P=(2,S_P,D_P),
 \qquad
 (A_L,D_L)=\mathsf{Lab}(Q_P),                             \tag{21}
\]
and
\[
 B_{k,\ell}
 =M_{k,\ell}
  (2+A_C+N_0+S_C+D_C)
  (1+A_P+2+S_P+D_P)
  (1+A_L+D_L).                                             \tag{22}
\]
Then \(B_{k,\ell}\) is explicit and computable and bounds both the total number of labeled outputs and every real-univariate algebraic degree produced by the compiler.  If \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\) and \(\operatorname{Exp}_2(x)=2^x\), the published bounds imply, for a universal constant \(C\ge1\), the conservative envelope
\[
 B_{k,\ell}
 \le
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(CQ^C\right)
 \right).                                                  \tag{23}
\]

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  For rational input coordinates of numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\), let \(\mathsf{Comp}_h\), \(\mathsf{Proj}_h\), and \(\mathsf{Lab}_h\) denote the corresponding published integer-coefficient height bounds, and define
\[
 h_0=B_{k,\ell}(L+1),\qquad
 h_C=\mathsf{Comp}_h(N_0,S_0,D_0,h_0),\qquad
 h_P=\mathsf{Proj}_h(Q_C,h_C),\qquad
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=\mathsf{Lab}_h(Q_P,h_P).                    \tag{24}
\]
After clearing guarded denominators, every algebraic target certificate can be represented by a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\), together with rational isolating endpoints whose coefficients and endpoints have binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  A Turing implementation therefore terminates.  Enlarging the same universal constant in (23) if necessary, the composed published height bounds give
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(CQ^C\right)
 \right)
 (L+1)^{\operatorname{Exp}_2(\operatorname{Exp}_2(CQ^C))}.\tag{25}
\]
The classification first enumerates the structural charts of \(\mathscr A\), then describes their connected components, and only then performs target projection and labeling; it does not report a generic two-copy quantifier-elimination test.
body.justification: The corrected theorem separates exact causal template counts from sequentially composed published component, projection, labeling, degree, and rational-height bounds.
body.gap: A generic decidability assertion neither counts the causal templates nor propagates one algorithm's output format into the next algorithm's input.
body.consumer: Symbolic implementations obtain an honest fixed-alphabet termination and exact-encoding contract over both oracle-real and rational input tiers.
body.proof_tex:
We verify (18)--(25) in the order in which the compiler executes its stages.

First consider the structural templates.  A vector \(b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) has nonempty support, so it has at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) labeled support patterns.  The four shared response vertices therefore contribute at most
\[
 (2^{\ell}-1)^4.                                           \tag{26}
\]
Positivity of \(p\) implies \(v_e(z)>0\) for every \((e,z)\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\), a rank-two cell has two orientations.  At a fixed \(z\), its two nonnegative incident coefficients sum to \(v_e(z)>0\), so exactly one of the following three support states holds: the first coefficient is zero, the second coefficient is zero, or both are positive.  Hence the rank-two charts contribute at most \(2\cdot 3^k\) local templates.  The same theorem and \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\) give \(3^k\) coordinatewise split faces in mode \(\mathrm E\), together with the three modes \(\mathrm L\), \(\mathrm R\), and \(\mathrm D\).  Thus, allowing either possible positive-table rank, the number of local templates for one cell is at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3.                               \tag{27}
\]
There are four response-cycle cells.  Multiplying (26) by the fourth power of (27) proves the formula for \(M_A\).

For design B, the residual-forest refinement of \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) assigns to each of the four response links either the zero-residual state or an active state.  An active state records one of the \(k-1\) lexicographically first nonbaseline pivots and one of its two signs.  It therefore has
\[
 1+2(k-1)=2k-1                                             \tag{28}
\]
states per link.  Relevance is certified by an unordered pair of distinct instrument values and the sign of the corresponding nonzero cross-product.  The number of such signed witnesses is
\[
 2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1).                                    \tag{29}
\]
Multiplication of \(M_A\), the fourth power of (28), and (29) proves the displayed formula for \(M_B\).  The two design-specific template families are disjoint outputs, so addition gives \(M_{k,\ell}=M_A+M_B\), proving (18).  Endpoint incidences and sign conditions not fixed by a structural template remain polynomial sign atoms within that template; their sign-invariant pieces and connected components are counted at the later stages rather than being omitted.

We next prove the uniform input-format bounds (19).  Retaining the four endpoint vectors uses \(4\ell\) coordinates, and retaining both incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells uses \(8k\) coordinates.  In design B, projective common-instrument coordinates together with optional \(q^X\) auxiliaries use at most \(2k\) further coordinates.  Population margins, response masses, and four residual-transfer scalars use at most twelve additional coordinates; their simplex and scale normalizations are equations and require no further coordinates.  Design A uses a subset of these coordinates.  Thus every chart has at most
\[
 N_0=4\ell+10k+12
\]
variables.

There are \(4k\ell\) table-factorization equations.  Endpoint-simplex and endpoint-support conditions contribute at most \(4\ell+4\) atoms; coefficient simplex, zero-pattern, and split-face conditions contribute at most \(24k+8\); and residual definitions and transfer equations contribute at most \(16k+8\).  If proportionality minors are retained in addition to, or instead of, transfer coordinates, they contribute at most \(4(k-1)^2\) atoms.  Shared-instrument equations, margin and response-mass normalizations, endpoint-incidence conditions, cycle consistency, and the signed relevance condition contribute fewer than \(20(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)\) further atoms.  Since \(k\ge2\) and \(\ell\ge3\), the sum of these displayed quantities is at most
\[
 S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1).
\]
The table-factorization equations are bilinear.  Each residual \(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0)\) has degree at most two.  With one transfer scalar on an active link, negative proportionality is expressed by equations of degree at most three, and an active four-link cycle gives a product equation of degree four.  The shared-instrument equations have degree two.  The relevance cross-product has degree at most three after substituting the defining bilinear expression for \(q^X\), and all simplex, support, normalization, and incidence atoms have no larger degree.  Hence \(D_0=4\), completing (19).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) to one template of format \((N_0,S_0,D_0)\).  By the definition of the coordinatewise nondecreasing bound \(\mathsf{Comp}\), the component stage returns at most \(A_C\) component records; each record is described in the original \(N_0\) ambient variables by at most \(S_C\) atoms of degree at most \(D_C\), and its sample uses at most one real-univariate primitive-element coordinate.  This proves the first equality in (20).

For each such record, the one-copy evaluator of \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) adjoins the two target coordinates, the two graph equations \(t=\tau_C\), and, when testing variation from the sampled value, one unequal-target condition.  Including the single primitive-element coordinate gives at most \(N_0+3\) variables and at most \(S_C+3\) atoms.  Clearing the guarded denominators introduced by the sample representation raises the degree to at most \(2D_C+2\).  Thus the actual next-stage input is bounded coordinatewise by
\[
 Q_C=(N_0+3,S_C+3,2D_C+2),
\]
which proves the second equality in (20).  Applying the one-block projection and realizability algorithm from \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) to this input, while retaining only the two target coordinates, gives
\[
 (A_P,S_P,D_P)=\mathsf{Proj}(Q_C;2),
 \qquad Q_P=(2,S_P,D_P).
\]
Applying the cited real-univariate, Thom-sign, comparison, and root-isolation algorithms to this actual projection output gives \((A_L,D_L)=\mathsf{Lab}(Q_P)\).  This proves (21) with the required sequential propagation of output format.

One initial structural template produces at most \(A_CA_PA_L\) labeled final records.  Across both designs their number is therefore at most
\[
 M_{k,\ell}A_CA_PA_L\le B_{k,\ell},                       \tag{30}
\]
because each of the three parenthesized factors in (22) dominates the corresponding positive output-count factor.  The first factor also dominates the component-description size and degrees, the second dominates the projection-description size and degrees, and the third dominates the final labeling degrees.  Consequently their product, with the structural multiplier, bounds both the total number of labeled outputs and every real-univariate degree produced at any stage.  This proves (22).  In particular, the chart count multiplies the per-chart sequential output bound; it is not replaced by a maximum.

Set \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\).  The formulas above give \(N_0=O(Q)\), \(S_0=O(Q)\), \(D_0=4\), and \(M_{k,\ell}\le 2^{Q^{c_0}}\) for a universal \(c_0\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}coarse\text{-}envelope}\), the component-stage count, atom count, and degree are each at most
\[
 (S_0+D_0+2)^{2^{c(N_0+1)^c}}
 \le 2^{2^{C_1Q^{C_1}}}                                  \tag{31}
\]
for a universal \(C_1\).  In the projection stage the ambient dimension is still at most \(N_0+3\), whereas the atom and degree inputs are bounded by (31).  Substitution into the same published envelope gives
\[
 (2+S_C+D_C)^{2^{c(N_0+4)^c}}
 \le 2^{2^{C_2Q^{C_2}}},                                 \tag{32}
\]
because raising a double-exponential base to a single-exponential exponent of polynomial size remains double exponential with a polynomial inner exponent.  The labeling stage has only two retained variables and inputs bounded by (32), so the same argument bounds its outputs by \(2^{2^{C_3Q^{C_3}}}\).  A fixed product of these factors and \(M_{k,\ell}\) has the same form after enlarging the universal constant.  Hence
\[
 B_{k,\ell}\le
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(CQ^C\right)
 \right),
\]
which proves (23).

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), every chart coefficient belongs to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Indeed, cell normalization divides only by the strictly positive observed margins \(r_e\), and every further chart division uses a pivot whose nonzero sign is recorded in that chart.  There are finitely many templates by (18).  Each component, projection, realizability, sign-determination, and real-root stage terminates by \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\), relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.  The complete field-relative computation therefore terminates.

Now suppose that every rational coordinate of \(\zeta\) has numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing deleted simplex coordinates, forming \(r_e\), and forming \(T_e=p_e/r_e\) require only the fixed-alphabet chart operations counted above.  Every denominator that is cleared is either positive by selected-table positivity or has a recorded nonzero sign; multiplying a sign condition by its square preserves that condition.  Since chart degrees are at most four and chart formula size is bounded by (22), ordinary integer numerator and denominator arithmetic bounds the resulting initial coefficient length by the conservative quantity
\[
 h_0=B_{k,\ell}(L+1).
\]
Applying the integer-height part of the component algorithm gives
\[
 h_C=\mathsf{Comp}_h(N_0,S_0,D_0,h_0).
\]
Feeding that actual height together with the actual component output format \(Q_C\) into the projection algorithm gives
\[
 h_P=\mathsf{Proj}_h(Q_C,h_C),
\]
and feeding the projection format and height into labeling and root isolation gives
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=\mathsf{Lab}_h(Q_P,h_P).
\]
This proves the sequential definitions in (24).  The square-free factorization and real-root-isolation parts of \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}components}\) then represent every algebraic target by a square-free integer polynomial and a rational isolating interval.  Its degree is at most \(B_{k,\ell}\) by (22), and all coefficient and endpoint lengths are at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\) by construction.

It remains to verify the displayed height envelope.  The height clause of \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}coarse\text{-}envelope}\) bounds each outgoing height by \((h+1)^R\), where the exponent \(R\) is controlled by the corresponding format bound.  By (31)--(32) and the labeling bound, all three successive exponents are at most \(2^{2^{C_4Q^{C_4}}}\) after increasing a universal \(C_4\).  Substituting successively in (24) multiplies only a fixed number of such exponents.  Since \(h_0\le 2^{2^{C_4Q^{C_4}}}(L+1)\) by (23), increasing the universal constant once more yields
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le
 \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(
   \operatorname{Exp}_2\!\left(CQ^C\right)
 \right)
 (L+1)^{\operatorname{Exp}_2(\operatorname{Exp}_2(CQ^C))},
\]
which is (25).  Every loop is now bounded and all rational-input subroutines are effective, so the Turing implementation terminates.

Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) proves that \(\mathscr A\) enumerates the structural charts first, computes their connected-component descriptions and samples second, and only then projects and labels the target.  Target variation is tested within a one-copy component description by refining it with \(\tau_C\ne t_0\), where \(t_0\) is its sampled target.  The causal interpretation and legal lifted outputs are supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:full\text{-}rigidity\text{-}atlas}\).  Thus the bounded procedure is the stated causal structural compiler and does not reduce the classification to generic two-copy quantifier elimination.
